raw_response:
I am already old, and with only 2 mu and just myself doing the work, I cannot make fancy plans. I will still do wheat and maize in rotation, same as before. On this little land, steady grain is more important than chasing high prices. I have farmed here many years, and around Quzhou this wheat-maize system is the safest. I have a well, so if the sky stays dry I can still save the crop, but pumping water costs money, so I will not irrigate too much. Since I only finished middle school, I listen to what the extension people say, but in the end I still follow what has worked on my own field. For wheat, I will put basal fertilizer before sowing, then topdress once at greening or jointing if the seedlings do not look strong. For maize, because it comes right after wheat and the turnaround is tight, I will keep it simple: quick residue clearing, light tillage, sow fast, put part of the fertilizer at planting and part later. I would rather spend a bit more on fertilizer than let the crop go yellow, but I still have to watch cash because this farm is small and every yuan counts.
